So we are still looking at a INR50 crores, INR55 crores target for our pharma, so which will be like almost a 50% growth over the last year number, INR34 crores, what we achieved.
So that's why I'm confident this year, we'll be crossing our target of INR42, INR43 we set for the full year.
Growth & demand: So now more than volume, I would look at -- one is definitely volume up to even 9%, 10% volume growth is equivalent to 14%, 15% of the past volume growth.
Sir, my first question is we are seeing 19% of our overall value growth, right, 6% volume growth while almost 19% growth in sales per kg.

Yes, I would always encourage people to look at the EBITDA per kg and of course, volume growth also as secondary because going forward, volume growth might be close to 10%, but EBITDA can grow around 18% to 20% also given our product mix changes and efficiencies that we are bringing in, in the operations.
Margins & costs: The turnover crossed INR300 crores, partially helped by increased raw material costs.
However, one of the most important points here is the per kg EBITDA has shot up to INR46.7 per kg, which is historically around INR40, INR42 was the best in the last several years.

So these are the reasons, and we could effectively pass on the price rise of raw material from -- if you notice the raw material cost, it was INR97 in the Q4 -- for the full year, INR107 in Q4, become INR130 now.
Capex & expansion: So we are still at the drawing table stage now, depending upon the plans, it could be 1 million pens per month will be the minimum capacity we'll be starting with.

And EBITDA growth of INR5 we achieved INR6, in fact, for the -- compared to the last year, full year at INR40.7, we did INR46.7 is mainly due to the consolidation and efficiencies and better capacity utilization, which will be long-term in nature.
Generally, after reaching a 75% capacity utilization, we generally look for a new capacity addition.
Balance sheet & cash: So overall working capital -- the raw material cost has shot up, if you compare it to last year, fourth quarter is INR97 average price is INR130.

That was the reason the interest has gone up considerably with increased raw material costs, inventory costs, we end up paying more working capital -- use more working capital and hence pay more interest on it.
So current working capital is INR125 crores, which was around INR110 crores, INR112 crores end of March, I think.
Risks & challenges: So only lubes are down due to the base oil disruption in a couple of our clients' locations.
Sir, my first question is that is it fair to say that we would have seen some volume decline.

Yes, there will be a capex of about INR90 crores for this current year, assuming INR25 crores to INR30 crores for pharma and the remaining for balancing and replacement.
